chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Muhammad ibn Awrama, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said:

I was a travel companion of Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi. When we were in al-Madinah, he went in to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, bid him farewell, and came out from him while he was cheerful, until we arrived at al-Ukhayrijah, the first stopping place on our route from Fayd to al-Madinah, on a Friday. We performed the midday salat, and when the camel rose to carry us on, I suddenly saw a tall dark-complexioned man carrying a letter. He handed it to Jabir, and Jabir took it, kissed it, placed it on his eyes, and it was from Muhammad ibn Ali to Jabir ibn Yazid, with wet black clay upon it.

He said to him, 'When were you last with my master?' He said, 'Just now.' He said to him, 'Before the salat or after the salat?' He said, 'After the salat.' So he broke the seal and began to read it, and his face tightened until he reached its end. Then he held the letter, and I did not see him laughing or cheerful until he arrived in al-Kufah. When we reached al-Kufah at night, I passed that night, and when morning came I went to him out of reverence for him. I found that he had come out to me with ankle bones hung around his neck, riding upon a reed, and saying, 'I find Mansur ibn Jumhur an amir not commanded,' and verses similar to this.

He looked into my face and I looked into his face, but he did not say anything to me, nor did I say anything to him. I began to weep because of what I saw of him, and children and people gathered around me and around him. He continued until he entered al-Rahbah and began moving about with the children, while the people were saying, 'Jabir ibn Yazid has gone mad, he has gone mad.'

By Allah, not many days passed before a letter from Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik came to his governor: 'Look for a man called Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, strike his neck, and send me his head.' So he turned to those sitting with him and said to them, 'Who is Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi?' They said, 'May Allah set you right, he was a man of knowledge, merit, and hadith, and he performed hajj; then he went mad, and there he is in al-Rahbah with the children, upon the reeds, playing with them.'

He said: So he looked down upon him, and there he was with the children playing upon the reeds. So he said, 'All praise is due to Allah, who spared me from killing him.' He said: And not many days passed until Mansur ibn Jumhur entered al-Kufah and did what Jabir had been saying.

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: Imam Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, from whom Jabir received guidance
key_terms.الرَّحَبَةَ: the open area where Jabir was seen among the children
key_terms.الْخَاتَمَ: the seal of the letter, which Jabir broke before reading
key_terms.الْكُوفَةَ: the city where Jabir's public display took place
key_terms.كِتَابٌ: a written message sent to Jabir
key_terms.مَنْصُورُ بْنُ جُمْهُورٍ: the figure whose later arrival fulfilled Jabir's words
key_terms.هِشَامِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ: the ruler who sent the order for Jabir's execution

ai.seo_question: How did Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi escape execution after receiving a letter from Imam Abu Ja'far عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates how Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi received a message from Imam Abu Ja'far عليه السلام and, after reading it, outwardly feigned madness. The report shows that this behavior preserved his life from a ruler's order to kill him, and it also reflects the Imam's foreknowledge of coming political events.
